description: Meet Wakayima the hare and Kintu, and tell a story’s lesson.

guidebook.intro: Ganda folktales (**enfumo**) are told in the evening. The two most famous are the tricks of **Wakayima** the hare, and the legend of **Kintu**, the first man.

phrases.base: What does this story teach us?
It teaches us that wisdom beats strength.

tips.title: Wakayima the trickster
body: The small hare beats bigger animals by cleverness: he tricks the elephant, the lion and the leopard. The lesson is usually **obugezi businga amaanyi** (wisdom beats strength), though sometimes Wakayima is caught out by his own lies.

tips.title: Kintu and Nnambi
body: **Kintu** lived alone with his cow until **Nnambi**, daughter of **Ggulu** (the sky), married him. Ggulu told them to leave quickly before her brother **Walumbe** (Death) could follow.
On the way, Nnambi went back for the millet she had forgotten for her chicken. **Walumbe** followed her, and that is why death came to the earth.

culture.title: Retelling
body: A good storyteller opens with **Olwatuuka olwali olumu**, gets the listeners to answer, and ends with the lesson: **Enfumo eno etuyigiriza nti…**. Now you can tell one too. Congratulations on reaching the last unit!

stories.title: Kintu and Nnambi
stories.summary: Jjajja tells Emma the legend of how death came to the earth.

line.speaker: emma
line.target: Jjajja, mpulira nti waliwo enfumo ya Kintu. Ngerera!
line.base: Grandma, I hear there is a story about Kintu. Tell me!

line.speaker: jjajja
line.target: Kale. Olwatuuka olwali olumu, Kintu ye muntu eyasooka. Yabeeranga yekka n’ente ye.
line.base: Well. Once upon a time, Kintu was the first person. He lived alone with his cow.

line.speaker: jjajja
line.target: Awo Nnambi, muwala wa Ggulu, n’amwagala. Kintu n’amuwasa.
line.base: Then Nnambi, the daughter of Ggulu, loved him. Kintu married her.

line.speaker: jjajja
line.target: Ggulu n’agamba nti: “Mugende mangu, Walumbe aleme okubagoberera.”
line.base: Ggulu said: “Go quickly, so that Death does not follow you.”

line.speaker: jjajja
line.target: Naye mu kkubo, Nnambi yeerabira obulo bw’enkoko. N’addayo.
line.base: But on the way, Nnambi forgot the chicken’s millet. She went back.

line.speaker: jjajja
line.target: Walumbe n’abagoberera ku nsi. Okuva olwo, abantu bafa.
line.base: Death followed them to the earth. Since then, people die.

line.speaker: emma
line.base: Oh! What does this story teach us?

line.speaker: jjajja
line.base: It teaches us that we should listen to elders.
